question: On 19 May 2026, Spain’s National High Court charged the former Spanish Prime Minister, José Luis Rodríguez Zapatero, with criminal association, influence peddling, money laundering and forgery of documents in connection with the EUR 53 million public bailout of Plus Ultra Líneas Aéreas in 2021. The aid was granted under a scheme authorised by the Commission (SA.59371, COVID-19 Temporary Framework).

The court order states that the beneficiaries acted ‘through mechanisms outside the legally established channels’ and that the airline itself paid for the technical reports supporting its classification as a ‘strategic’ company.

In 2024, the Spanish Court of Auditors found that the Spanish state-owned industrial holding company, Sociedad Estatal de Participaciones Industriales, had breached its obligation to provide a report to the Commission on the Solvency Support Fund for Strategic Companies in 2022. In view of the above: 1.

Will the Commission reopen case SA.59371 and require the aid to be fully recovered in accordance with Article 16 of Regulation (EU) 2015/1589 if it is confirmed that it was granted as a result of false information?
Will the Commission refer the case to the European Public Prosecutor’s Office so that it can assess whether it is competent for the matter under Article 22(3) of Regulation (EU) 2017/1939?
Will it open infringement proceedings against Spain for failure to provide information, as identified by the Spanish Court of Auditors?
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (23.7.2026) The Commission does not wish to speculate on the ongoing judicial inquiries regarding the airline Plus Ultra.

The Commission does not currently have any information that would justify either reopening the case or revoking its decision of 31 July 2020 authorising the recapitalisation aid scheme in question, the legality of which has been confirmed by the General Court and the Court of Justice of the European Union1.

The Commission recalls that, in accordance with Article 22 of Regulation (EU) 2017/19392, the material competence of the European Public Prosecutor’s Office is limited to criminal offences affecting the financial interests of the European Union that are provided for in Directive (EU) 2017/1371.

The Commission’s decision referred to above specifies that the aid scheme in question has been funded by the Spanish State budget. In these circumstances, the question of whether a criminal offence may have been committed does not seem relevant in light of the ongoing judicial inquiries.
1 State Aid SA.57659(2020/N) - Spain COVID 19 - Recapitalisation fund. OJ C/2020/269, 14.8.2020, p. 8. Cases

T-628/20 EU:T:2021:514 and C-441/21 P, EU:C:2024:447. 2 Council Regulation (EU) 2017/1939 of 12 October 2017 implementing enhanced cooperation on the establishment of the European Public Prosecutor’s Office (the EPPO), OJ L 283, 31.10.2017, p.1.
